To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the YAP/TEF transcriptional regulators and microRNA-130-5p/301a-3p act in a feedback circuit to promote fibrosis across a broad spectrum of human physiologies and pathologies, and that this mechanism may represent a new therapeutic target in fibrotic diseases.
a YAP/TAz-miR-301 molecular circuit controls fibrosis across a network of seemingly disparate diseases.
a microRNA-130-301 family and YAP/TEF co-transcription factors form a molecular circuit that exerts systems-level controls of tissue fibrosis in a broad network of human diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of fibrosis, a process in which the normal structure and function of a tissue is lost.
understanding the molecular basis of disease.
the molecular mechanisms of fibrosis, a pathological process that is a common feature of multiple tissue beds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the YAP/taZ-MicroRNA-130/30I Molecular Circuit Exerts System-level Control of Fibrosis in a Network of Human Diseases and Physiologic Conditions.
the molecular origins of fibrotic disease are not unique to the tissue bed in which they manifest, but rather are dictated by the shared molecular circuit of YAP/TAz and the miR-130/30 family.
the molecular origins of fibrotic tissue stiffening are common across multiple tissue beds, and are dictated by the YAP- and TAZ-dependent regulation of the microRNA-301 family.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown how a single molecular circuit, the microRNA-30/301-YAP/TAZ circuit, is responsible for the induction of fibrosis in seemingly disparate tissue beds, including the lung, liver, kidney, heart, and skin, and that the inhibition of this circuit can prevent fibrosis in two of these tissue beds, the lung and liver.

we have identified a common molecular circuitry that is responsible for the fibrotic phenotype in a network of seemingly disparate diseases, which is based on the mechanistic interplay between microRNAs and YAP/ TAZ.

we have identified the microRNA-301/130 family, and its upstream regulator YAP/TAz, as master regulators of fibrosis in pulmonary hypertension and pulmonary fibrosis, and potentially in liver fibrosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single master regulator, microRNA-130a/301a, can exert a systems-level control of tissue fibrosis across seemingly disparate disease and physiologic contexts.
the molecular circuitry of the microRNA-301/130 and the co-transcriptional factor YAP/TAz is conserved and exerts systems level control of fibrosis across a wide network of human diseases.
the microRNA-301 family is a master regulator of ECM remodeling and fibrosis across multiple tissue beds and disease states.
